project.name: BrowseSight
project.core_idea: BrowseSight is a browser extension that helps users understand whether a link, website, or email is safe at the exact moment they are about to interact with it. It identifies scams, phishing attempts, impersonation, and privacy risks using threat intelligence and AI, and presents this risk clearly without blocking access or forcing decisions.
project.detailed_description: BrowseSight acts as a real-time trust intelligence layer across Google Search, websites, and Gmail. It focuses on clarity, timing, and user behavior by providing visual cues, simple explanations, and contextual guidance at decision points while fully respecting user autonomy and privacy.

milestones.backend_api_v2_0_1: Successfully developed a high-performance Express.js central server integrating Google Safe Browsing, VirusTotal, and Groq AI.
milestones.ai_risk_assessment: Implemented advanced URL pattern analysis using Groq AI (Llama 3.3 70B) to catch zero-day phishing and suspicious domains with ~100% detection rate.
milestones.high_availability: Built a robust AI failover system with primary and backup Groq API keys for 100% uptime.

groq_api.purpose: AI inference for scam classification, intent detection, language analysis, and behavioral understanding

virustotal_api.purpose: Domain and URL reputation intelligence using multiple security engines

openai_api.purpose: Human-readable explanations and scam summaries (optional, can use Groq instead)

browser_extension_apis.purpose: UI injection, navigation monitoring, user interaction handling, local storage

search_and_website: Hover-Scan (On-Demand): Analyzes links only when hovered.
Instant-Response Architecture: Server-side caching and fast-path logic for <200ms results.
Surgical UI: Status dots vertically aligned with text, breadcrumbs ignored.
reporting_and_evidence: Threat Intelligence Report (PDF) — Formal multi-section report with unique Report ID and IST timestamp, suitable for submission to CERT-In, cybercrime.gov.in, VirusTotal, and PhishTank

steps: User clicks Download and the ZIP file is saved locally
User extracts the ZIP file to obtain the extension folder
User opens Chrome and navigates to chrome://extensions
User enables Developer mode (one-time Chrome requirement)
User clicks Load unpacked and selects the extracted folder
BrowseSight extension is installed and becomes active immediately
user_experience_notes: No silent permissions or background installs
Developer mode can be turned off after installation
first_run_behavior: Extension icon appears in the browser toolbar
BrowseSight runs silently in the background
Visual indicators appear only when risk is detected
No websites or actions are blocked

backend_server.description: Express.js API server that aggregates threat intelligence from multiple sources and provides analysis endpoints for the browser extension. Features parallel execution of security checks for ~2s response times.
backend_server.architecture: The extension communicates with the backend API server, which securely stores all API keys and handles requests to external threat intelligence services

url_analysis.purpose: Analyze URLs for scams, phishing, and security risks

email_analysis.purpose: Analyze email content for phishing and scam indicators

security.cors: Configured to allow browser extension origins
security.api_key_storage: All external API keys stored securely in environment variables, never exposed to users

api_server.purpose: Backend API server that the extension calls for threat analysis

landing_page.purpose: Public website where users download the extension and learn about features

yellow_list.definition: The yellow list represents high-level future features that demonstrate long-term vision. These features are intentionally excluded from the core build and are not claimed as implemented.

presentation_notes_for_teammate.major_talking_point_1: The BrowseSight API is now fully developed (v2.0.1) and production-ready, serving as the 'brain' of the extension.
presentation_notes_for_teammate.major_talking_point_2: AI Integration is a game-changer: We use Groq AI (Llama 3) to analyze URL naming psychology and patterns, which catches phishing sites that aren't in any database yet.
presentation_notes_for_teammate.major_talking_point_3: Deep Scan Capability: The extension now scans the entire source code of websites to find malicious links hidden in common UI elements like buttons and download links.
presentation_notes_for_teammate.ppt_requirement: Include a dedicated slide for the 'AI Integration & Multi-Source Intelligence' explaining how we combine Google, VirusTotal, and Groq for a 100% detection rate path.
